title: Subquadratic Architectures: xLSTM vs. Mamba-2 vs. Gated DeltaNet
hook: Transformers pay a quadratic tax on sequence length. Pitting xLSTM, Mamba-2, and Gated DeltaNet head-to-head on hard tasks, xLSTM comes out ahead — and the paper explains why.
key_points: Subquadratic architectures avoid attention's quadratic cost; the open question is which design actually models sequences best.
The study compares xLSTM, Mamba-2, and Gated DeltaNet on code pretraining, code-model distillation, and time-series foundation-model pretraining.
xLSTM delivers the strongest overall performance across these settings.
A unified formulation traces xLSTM's edge to more flexible, stable memory correction via its gating scheme.
Controlled length-generalization tasks confirm the gains come from robust state tracking and accumulation.
content_html: Transformers dominate sequence modeling, but their quadratic attention is expensive, and subquadratic architectures promise a more scalable alternative. The catch, the authors note, is that it's unclear which subquadratic design actually models sequences best. They run a head-to-head comparison of three leading approaches — xLSTM, Mamba-2, and Gated DeltaNet — on tasks with complex dependencies: code-model pretraining, distillation of code models from LLMs, and pretraining of time-series foundation models.
extra_html: Across these settings, xLSTM delivers the strongest overall performance. To explain why, the authors present a unified formulation and analyze the underlying mechanisms, focusing on state tracking and memory dynamics. Their account: xLSTM's gating scheme enables more flexible and stable memory correction than its rivals, and controlled synthetic length-generalization tasks corroborate that its gains stem from robust state tracking and accumulation. The card-sized takeaway is that, among modern recurrence/state-space designs, how a model corrects and accumulates its hidden state — not just that it's subquadratic — is what separates the strong from the merely fast.

related.title: Feature Learning in Gated Delta Networks at Scale
related.hook: muP lets you tune hyperparameters on a small model and transfer them to a huge one. This paper derives the equivalent rules for gated delta networks, so sub-quadratic models scale without re-tuning.

related.title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
related.hook: Make the state-space transitions depend on the input itself, add a hardware-aware scan, and you get a linear-time sequence model that matches Transformers on language - with no KV cache.

related.title: Nemotron 3 Ultra: Open Hybrid Mamba-Attention MoE
related.hook: NVIDIA's open 550B model interleaves Mamba and attention inside a Mixture-of-Experts - hitting ~6x the inference throughput of comparable LLMs at on-par accuracy.

flashcards.prompt: Why study subquadratic architectures at all?
flashcards.back_html: Transformer attention scales quadratically with sequence length; subquadratic models (xLSTM, Mamba-2, Gated DeltaNet) aim to model long sequences without that cost.

flashcards.prompt: Among xLSTM, Mamba-2, and Gated DeltaNet, which gave the strongest overall results in this study?
flashcards.explanation_html: Across code pretraining, code-model distillation, and time-series pretraining, xLSTM was strongest — the paper credits its gating-based memory correction.

flashcards.prompt: What mechanism does the paper credit for xLSTM's advantage?
flashcards.back_html: Its gating scheme, which enables more flexible and stable memory correction — yielding robust state tracking and accumulation on tasks with complex dependencies.
